importantNotes: The Passover lamb foreshadows Christ as the Lamb of God (John 1:29).
The Ten Commandments reveal God's moral standard for His people.
The Tabernacle represents God's desire to dwell among His people.
Moses is a type of Christ — deliverer, mediator, and lawgiver.

chapters.1: Israel multiplies in Egypt; Pharaoh enslaves them and orders the killing of Hebrew baby boys.
chapters.2: Moses is born, hidden in a basket, and raised by Pharaoh's daughter; he later flees to Midian.
chapters.3: God appears to Moses in the burning bush and commissions him to deliver Israel.
chapters.4: God gives Moses signs to perform; Moses returns to Egypt with Aaron.
chapters.5: Moses confronts Pharaoh; Pharaoh increases Israel's labor burden.
chapters.6: God reaffirms His covenant and promises deliverance; genealogy of Moses and Aaron.
chapters.7: Aaron's staff becomes a snake; the first plague — water turned to blood.
chapters.8: Plagues of frogs, gnats, and flies strike Egypt.
chapters.9: Plagues on livestock, boils, and hail devastate Egypt.
chapters.10: Plagues of locusts and darkness cover the land of Egypt.
chapters.11: God announces the final plague — death of every firstborn in Egypt.
chapters.12: The Passover is instituted; the firstborn of Egypt die; Israel leaves Egypt.
chapters.13: Consecration of the firstborn; God leads Israel with a pillar of cloud and fire.
chapters.14: God parts the Red Sea; Israel crosses on dry ground; the Egyptian army is destroyed.
chapters.15: Moses and Miriam sing a victory song; bitter waters at Marah are made sweet.
chapters.16: God provides manna and quail to feed Israel in the wilderness.
chapters.17: Water from the rock at Horeb; Israel defeats the Amalekites with Moses' raised arms.
chapters.18: Jethro advises Moses to appoint judges to share the burden of leadership.
chapters.19: Israel arrives at Mount Sinai; God descends on the mountain in fire and thunder.
chapters.20: God gives the Ten Commandments to Israel.
chapters.21: Laws about servants, personal injury, and property rights.
chapters.22: Laws about property, social responsibility, and justice.
chapters.23: Laws about justice, Sabbath, festivals, and the angel who will guide Israel.
chapters.24: The covenant is confirmed; Moses, Aaron, and the elders see God; Moses ascends Sinai.
chapters.25: Instructions for the Ark of the Covenant, the table of showbread, and the golden lampstand.
chapters.26: Instructions for building the Tabernacle with curtains and frames.
chapters.27: Instructions for the altar of burnt offering and the courtyard of the Tabernacle.
chapters.28: Instructions for the priestly garments of Aaron and his sons.
chapters.29: Instructions for the consecration of the priests.
chapters.30: Instructions for the altar of incense, the basin, and the anointing oil.
chapters.31: Bezalel and Oholiab are chosen as skilled craftsmen; Sabbath regulations.
chapters.32: Israel worships the golden calf; Moses breaks the stone tablets in anger.
chapters.33: God threatens to withdraw His presence; Moses pleads and sees God's glory.
chapters.34: God renews the covenant; new stone tablets; Moses' face shines.
chapters.35: The people bring offerings for the Tabernacle; work begins.
chapters.36: The skilled workers construct the Tabernacle curtains and frames.
chapters.37: Construction of the Ark, the table, the lampstand, and the incense altar.
chapters.38: Construction of the altar of burnt offering, the basin, and the courtyard.
chapters.39: The priestly garments are made; all the Tabernacle work is completed.
chapters.40: The Tabernacle is erected; the glory of the LORD fills it.
